request.spec:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their cut total: their cuts across every pool they are a member of, added
up (a pool that shows no cuts adds nothing). Show the sheet's cut total: everyone's added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The cut totals are in place, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

- **Each person:** the people table has a new "Cut total" column (`person-cut-total`). It adds up the cuts the person has in every pool they belong to. A pool that shows no cut adds nothing — for example, a pool that isn't balanced or has no pot. A retired member's cut already counts as 0.00.
- **The sheet:** a "Cut total" line (`rollup-cut-total`) adds up the cuts of every person in the pools. Pools that are members of other pools are skipped, so no cut is counted twice.

The change is front-end only, in `features/pools/pools.ts` and `features/pools/pools.slot.tsx`. The pools API already returned each member's cut, so the totals are added up from that data, with the sums done in whole cents. The data, the server and the audit file are unchanged, and the spec doesn't expect any new audit records.

The sheet total counts every person listed in the pools, not only the people shown in the table. These match the per-person totals unless someone in a pool can be missing from the people list. The tests don't cover that case, and I didn't check whether it can happen.
